A Guide to Understanding Startup Stock Options

This guide explains how stock options work for employees at early stage companies.
For illustrative purposes, suppose an employee is granted 10,000 stock options with an exercise price of $2.00 per share.
In this example the company later sells for $12.00 per share, and the options vest over four years with a one year cliff.
The hypothetical employee would exercise 10,000 shares at a cost of $20,000, which is 0.10% of the fully diluted company.
Let's say the base salary in this example is $140,000 per year.
Your own grant will differ, so read your documents with care and talk to a qualified advisor.
